exposure: prolonged second stage of labor (> 3 h)
cohort: 368 live newborns born at Jimma zone public hospitals, enrolled using systematic random sampling.
finding: Birth asphyxia was significantly associated with several factors including medical and obstetric complications, prolonged second stage of labor, low birth weight, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, tight nuchal cord, inadequate antenatal care, non-cephalic presentation, and caesarian section delivery.
mod_finding: Caesarian section delivery was associated with birth asphyxia (AOR: 2.3, 95%CI: 1.0, 5.1).
birth_weight: Low birth weight was associated with birth asphyxia (AOR 4.21, 95%CI 1.5, 12.2)
